Card.title: Player card
Card.lead: Hover over the card or tap it to flip it.
bio: From Talas, lives in Bishkek. Middle Frontend Developer at Tunduk, building government services used by people all over the country.
Studies information security at college, so he thinks not only about how a form looks but also about what someone might send through it.
Has already closed backend tasks on a work project, and wants to play in that position for good.

Scout.title: Scouting report
Scout.strengths: Careful typing, responsive layouts, accessible interfaces, an eye for form security.
Scout.growing: Node.js, SQL, API design and working with databases.
Scout.note: Sometimes writes CSS at 3 a.m. The coaching staff are aware.

Match.title: Career as a match
Match.lead: Scroll down: the clock on the scoreboard runs with you.
fouls: Yellow card to Bugs for diving: “works on my machine”.
Second yellow, that’s red! Bugs are sent off. Until the next release.
Bugs are already in the dressing room. The referee asks not to disturb them.
commentary: Alisher beats three bugs and is one on one with production!
The referee shows a yellow card for !important in CSS.
VAR is checking: bug or feature? Feature. Play on.
The coach shouts from the touchline: “Type it!”
The ball hits the post. The post turns out to be legacy code.
Match stats: zero console.log in production. Almost.

Projects.title: Projects
Projects.lead: What he has worked on, in brief.

kcaPublic.description: The public portal of a government service. Application forms with validation, a personal account and a responsive layout that works as well on a phone as on a desktop.

kcaAdmin.description: An internal panel for staff: sortable, filterable tables, roles and permissions. Also where he took his first backend tasks, in kca-backend.

weather.description: Weather for the cities of Kyrgyzstan: temperature and precipitation charts, dark theme.

portfolio.description: Next.js with static generation: content is rendered on the server and interactivity is layered on top. Every sound is synthesised in the browser with the Web Audio API.
